title: Sessions with a special education specialist
what: A specialist helps a child with a developmental delay learn to talk, understand, think, and play. Sessions are done through play.
why: When a child is behind in speech, attention, or understanding, and with hearing or vision problems, autism, or cerebral palsy.
duration: a session usually takes 30 to 45 minutes, and you need to attend regularly for months
tell_doctor: What worries you about your child's development
What your child can already do: words, games, self-care
Reports from other doctors and specialists
How your child sleeps, eats, and behaves at home
Whether they go to kindergarten or school

prepare.title: Routine
prepare.text: Plan the session for when your child is rested and has eaten.

prepare.title: Talking
prepare.text: Tell your child they are going to play with a new grown-up.

prepare.title: Notes
prepare.text: Write down what you notice at home, which makes it easier to tell the specialist.

steps: The specialist gets to know your child through play
Watches how your child understands speech, plays, and does tasks
Tells you what is going well and what needs developing
Makes a plan for the sessions
Works with your child following the plan
Shows you how to continue at home
feel: Your child may feel shy or fussy the first time, which is normal
Progress can be slow, but it happens
after: Repeat at home what you were shown
Talk to your doctor and the specialist if something changes

faq.q: How is this different from a speech therapist?
faq.a: A speech therapist mostly works on speech. This specialist develops thinking, attention, understanding, and play together with speech.

faq.q: From what age can we start?
faq.a: The earlier, the better. There are sessions even for children under three.

reminders.text: Your child's session with the specialist is today. Bring a favorite toy and a snack.
